content.text:
The malicious document came from **galmon.com**. I wrote that to `../shared/answers/agent_0.txt`.

The evidence is a single chain on WS-903 (user luis.munoz):
- **08:51:00Z**: proxy shows `GET http://galmon.com/invoice_12052.docm`, action **allowed** (183 KB returned). DNS resolved galmon.com at 08:50:58Z.
- **08:52:00Z**: `winword.exe` opens `C:\Users\luis.munoz\Downloads\invoice_12052.docm`, spawned from `outlook.exe`.
- **08:52:20Z**: `winword.exe` spawns `powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc ...`, a hidden encoded PowerShell launch typical of a malicious macro.
- **09:07:00Z** onward: the same host runs `svchelper.exe /collect /out C:\Users\Public\sv.dat` and beacons to bexfirsky.com/api/v2/sync every few minutes.

The other `.docm` download, `datgal.co/statement_958.docm` from WS-589 at 08:12, was **blocked** and shows no follow-on execution, so it is a look-alike that did not start the intrusion. I found no earlier document-based execution in the logs.

I also appended the finding to `../shared/NOTES.md`. A stray directory I created by mistake at `logtest/shared` during the first write attempt has been removed.

**Answer:** `galmon.com`
